name: King of Dor
overview: The King of Dor was a male ruler identified as one of the thirty-one kings defeated by Joshua during the conquest of Canaan. Scripture does not specify his tribal affiliation or provide additional personal details. His role is primarily noted within the context of Israel's military victories under Joshua's leadership.
namesAndTitles: The title 'King of Dor' directly denotes his position as the ruler of the city-state of Dor. The name carries no special Hebrew or Greek meaning beyond its literal designation as the king governing Dor, as recorded in Joshua 12:23.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture does not record any family relationships for the King of Dor beyond his identification as a defeated monarch in the conquest narratives. No additional relational details are provided.
scriptureSignificance: The King of Dor serves as a representative figure among the Canaanite kings who opposed Israel's divinely sanctioned conquest under Joshua. His defeat signifies God's faithfulness in granting victory to His people over the established powers in the land. This highlights the fulfillment of God's promises to Israel and the establishment of His covenantal purposes through Joshua's leadership.
